terms.grammar: rotō, rotāre, rotāvī, rotātum, with corpus as its object
evidence: M-O s.v. somersaults: do somersaults, turn cartwheels (Bauer, Helfer)
terms.comment: Morgan–Owens gives it for the German radschlagen, turn cartwheels, from Bauer and Helfer, beside cernuāre for the somersault (see “somersault”). Rotāre, whirl a thing round like a wheel, is poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: turn a cartwheel, roll oneself over like a wheel
terms.grammar: volvō with the reflexive; in modum with the genitive
terms.comment: A description of ours, for explaining the turn: in modum with the genitive, “in the manner of”, and sē volvere, roll oneself.

phrases.english: Watch me: I’m doing a cartwheel!

phrases.latin: Prīmum manūs in terram pōne, deinde crūra in altum jace.
phrases.english: First put your hands on the ground, then throw your legs up.

sources: Lewis & Short: roto · Lewis & Short: rota · Lewis & Short: volvo
